title: Training law enforcement interviewers to mitigate resistance using rapport- and trust-based approaches
abstract: Objectives Science-based interviewing is an empirically validated alternative to traditional accusatory interviewing techniques that too often lead to investigative failures. A barrier to implementation has been the lack of research that addresses resistance in interview subjects. Methods We trained 139 experienced investigators on how to recognize and mitigate resistance by using a rapport- and trust-based model of interviewing. We evaluated the effectiveness of this science-based training using a quasi-experimental pre/post design. We examined investigators’ attitudes, learning, and behavior, immediately after the training, six months and one year later. Results Investigators found the training beneficial and relevant. Trainee knowledge assessments indicated an increased use of science-based and decreased use of traditional techniques post-training. Trainees indicated an intent to use more science-based interviewing techniques post-training. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate that a training focused on resistance mitigation that incorporates science-based tactics resulted in increased knowledge and willingness to use such tactics in the field.
